items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: like Rudy Wiedoft and Benny End [?] and so forth

ctx.x: Oh, I heard a band with a guy named Leonard Fields, saxophone player and I don't know exactly who was drumming [?] for them. The trumpet player was a guy who used to go around with Sugar Ray Robinson as a valet or something. He played like Louie Armstrong, he sounded like Louie Armstrong and he tried, you see. I can't think of his name now, he was playing just like Louie Armstrong, I mean copy, you know, see. He was really inspired and had that voice all the time, in the street. I just can't pin his name. Well…

think he's named Leonard - had the fastest tongue of any negro saxophone player, and I watched it - why I say negro, because when they come down to fast tongues, you go back to the virtuoso, and them virtuosos were white, most of them, you know. 100, 80 per cent, 90 per cent of all of virtuosos on the saxophone were white, you know. And - like Rudy Wiedoft and Benny End [?] and so forth, you now, see. And they - that's their thing, that terrific attack on the, with the tongue, see. And this Leonard Fields, that's…
You're saying - why did you bring in Benny Carter's name on this?
